Exact actions, approvals and portable evidence MPAS represents a requested action as an Action Package: the execution payload, an envelope that binds it by a cryptographic digest, and approvals. A proposer requests the action, signers review it and a deterministic verifier decides whether the package satisfies policy. Native verification and a credential adapter are alternative integration routes; the adapter is useful when the target does not verify MPAS directly. The digest ties approval to the data that will run. Rechecking it can detect payload substitution; it does not establish that a display faithfully explained the action or that the action is wise. Authorization says what may happen. A receipt reports an outcome. Transporting either object does not by itself establish execution.
